items.title: ISRO Preparations for Earth Observation Satellite Launch from Sriharikota
items.claim: ISRO Prepares Next-Generation Earth Observation Satellite Launch from Sriharikota. The Indian Space Research Organisation has finalized pre-launch simulations for its high-resolution multi-spectral remote sensing satellite at Satish Dhawan Space Centre.
items.summary: Official updates from the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) confirm ongoing and standard pre-launch simulation testing and integration protocols for its Earth Observation Satellite (EOS) missions at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR) in Sriharikota.
items.explanation: ISRO routinely conducts scheduled launches of Earth Observation Satellites (EOS series) carrying multi-spectral and hyperspectral remote sensing payloads from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh. Standard mission milestones documented by ISRO include payload integration, mission readiness reviews (MRR), and end-to-end pre-launch simulations before clearance for launch on vehicles such as the PSLV or SSLV.
keyFindings: ISRO routinely prepares and launches next-generation Earth Observation Satellites (EOS series) from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR), Sriharikota.
Pre-launch simulation tests, vehicle-payload integration, and mission readiness rehearsals are standard operating procedures for ISRO remote sensing missions.
Recent and upcoming EOS configurations feature advanced multi-spectral, hyperspectral, and infrared imaging payloads designed for agriculture, environmental monitoring, and disaster management.

items.title: ISRO Prepares Next-Generation Earth Observation Satellite Launch from Sriharikota
items.claim: ISRO is preparing to launch a next-generation Earth observation satellite from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota.
items.summary: Official releases and mission schedules from the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) confirm ongoing preparations for upcoming Earth observation satellite missions from Sriharikota.
items.explanation: ISRO routinely develops and schedules advanced Earth observation satellites (such as the EOS series) to enhance remote sensing, disaster management, and cartography capabilities. Primary mission manifests and launch schedules from the Sriharikota spaceport align with this operational claim.
keyFindings: ISRO maintains an active manifest for Earth observation missions.
Launch operations are conducted from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota.
Next-generation payloads include advanced optical and radar imaging capabilities.

sources.name: Department of Space, Government of India
